title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is mostly figures. Its mathematical content is a small bookkeeping computation tied to the regular-map (carte) material on the neighbouring pages. Reading the formulas and labels together, the setting appears to be as follows.

(1) Labels. Three objects R_1, R_2, R_3 are indexed by Z/3. The symbol omega (or omega' = omega^2) acts on indices by cyclic shift i -> omega i, which defines an orientation of the triangle (i, j, k). The differences are Q_i^omega = R_j - R_k = R_{omega i} - R_{omega^2 i}, so Q_i^{omega'} = -Q_i^omega. This matches the pair of labels Q_i^{omega'}, Q_i^{omega^2} drawn at the two ends of a small meridian circle on the torus.

(2) Twisting. Each difference is twisted by a root of unity zeta. The small figure shows the unit circle with 1, -1 and an arc from 1 to zeta. This gives Q_i^omega = R_j - R_k |-> P_i^{omega,zeta} = R_j - zeta R_k. At zeta = 1 one recovers Q_i; at zeta = -1 one would get R_j + R_k, which equals -R_i if sum R_i = 0. Grothendieck notes that P_i^{omega,zeta} takes 12 distinct values: six for fixed zeta (the P_i^omega, i in Z/3, omega in {omega, omega'}, with signs) and six more. The last formula, P_i^{omega',zeta'} = R_k - zeta^2 R_j = -zeta' P_i^{omega,zeta}, is consistent only if zeta' = zeta^{-1} = zeta^2. So zeta is apparently a primitive cube root of unity, and reversing orientation multiplies by a root of unity.

(3) The 12-gon. The 12 values, labelled ±R_i^omega and ±R_i^{omega'}, are placed cyclically on a 12-gon with rays to a centre, i.e. the cone or star of a regular 12-gon. Arrows pair adjacent vertices: R_2^omega <-> R_2^{omega'}, -R_1^omega <-> -R_1^{omega'}, R_3^omega <-> R_3^{omega'}, and so on. This is the same kind of object as the previous page's regular maps Sigma_n of polygons, with dihedral symmetry D_n and D_{2n}. Here n = 12 or 6, the symmetry being generated by omega (order 3), the sign (order 2) and zeta.

(4) The torus figure. The torus is drawn with:
- marked points Q_1, Q_2, Q_3 on one parallel;
- points R_1, R_2, R_3, each with a small circle carrying two 'tangential' points R_{i,omega}, R_{i,omega'} and rotation arrows;
- for each i, a small cylinder or box with corners R_i^omega, R_i^{omega'}, -R_i^omega, -R_i^{omega'} and a middle point \tilde R_i;
- meridian circles at Q_1 and Q_3.
This looks like a cell decomposition or real-oriented-blow-up picture: each special point is replaced by a boundary circle carrying the 'directions' omega, omega'. The apparent aim is to build a regular map or dessin on a torus (or a cyclic arrangement of 12 cells) with the order-3/order-6 symmetry, and to read the cartographic-group action on it. The next page sets up exactly this formalism: flags r = (s, a, f), involutions tau_0, tau_1, tau_infinity, and rotations rho_0, rho_1, rho_infinity.

The precise identity of the R_i is not stated on the page: 2-torsion points, roots of a cubic, or vertices of a map. The interpretation above is therefore partly conjectural.
errors: The identity P_i^{omega,zeta} = -P_{omega^2 i}^{omega,zeta} does not hold as written. With P_i^{omega,zeta} = R_{omega i} - zeta R_{omega^2 i}, one gets P_{omega^2 i} = R_i - zeta R_{omega i}, which is not -P_i in general. Either an index or a factor of zeta is missing, or the right-hand side belongs to a different line.

In P_i^{omega',zeta'} = R_k - zeta^2 R_j = -zeta' P_i^{omega,zeta}, the middle term needs zeta' = zeta^{-1} = zeta^2, i.e. zeta must be a primitive cube root of unity. For a general zeta on the unit circle (as the circle sketch suggests), the correct middle term is R_k - zeta^{-1} R_j. The assumption on zeta is never stated.

ideas.what: Twisting differences R_j - R_k of three cyclically indexed points by a root of unity zeta, producing 12 points with an action of mu_3 x {±1} x <zeta>, arranged as a 12-gon.
ideas.modern_name: orbit computation for a regular map / dessin with cyclic-dihedral symmetry (hexagonal-type map on a j=0 torus, if that is the setting)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (regular maps: Coxeter-Moser; dessins: Grothendieck 1984, Jones-Singerman 1978)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme treats regular maps and dessins in general, not this specific computation

ideas.what: Replacing marked points on a surface by small circles carrying tangential 'direction' points (R_{i,omega}, R_{i,omega'}) and meridians at Q_i.
ideas.modern_name: real oriented blow-up / tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne 1989 (tangential base points); Kawazumi, Kontsevich (oriented blow-ups)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse mentions 'points base' and tangential considerations for M_{0,4} only informally

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working page of figures and a small index computation (orbit of 12 points under omega, sign and a root of unity), feeding the regular-map and cartographic-group material on the adjacent pages. It contains no new result or unexplored connection beyond what the general dessins/regular-maps program already contains.
transcription_corrections: In the formula P_i^{omega,zeta} = R_{omega i} - zeta R_{omega^? i}, the second index reads like omega^2 i (possibly overwritten as omega^4 i); the crossed-out zeta after R_{omega i} is correctly marked.
The torus label transcribed as 'R_{2,omega}^{omega} [?]' is better read as R_{2,omega'}^{omega} (lower right corner of the R_2 box), and '-R^{omega'}_2' sits next to R_2 at the bottom of the box.
The text line is better read as: 'P_i^{omega,zeta} prend 12 valeurs distinctes / P_i six valeurs pour zeta fixé (les P_i^omega) et les six [autres]'.
